text.tspan: llm-capacity-planner --help
Which NVIDIA hardware a Hugging Face model needs with vLLM or SGLang, how many users it serves,
and how fast. Nothing is downloaded or run: only config.json and safetensors headers are read.
No GPU and no inference engine are needed on this computer.
Examples (free models, no license to accept; they work offline from the built-in data):
llm-capacity-planner zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tokens 128k --users 200
long documents (128k tokens ≈ 200 pages), 200 users
llm-capacity-planner moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code --tokens 128k --users 300 --active 30
coding with agents, 300 users at 30% active (agents are busy)
llm-capacity-planner zai-org/GLM-5.3 --users 200
the same 200 users at the model's maximum context (1M tokens)
llm-capacity-planner openai/gpt-oss-120b --tokens 32k --users 2000 --prompt-cache 80
chat, 2,000 users, 80% of each request already in the prefix cache
llm-capacity-planner deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 --tokens 64k --gpu h200 --count 8 --details
one configuration in detail: 8× H200, every number and its limits
llm-capacity-planner zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tokens 128k --users 200 --engine sglang
the same question for the SGLang engine
llm-capacity-planner report glm --csv glm.csv
ready-made results for recent open models (here: the GLM ones), saved for Excel
The three main options:
model
the Hugging Face repo id, e.g. zai-org/GLM-5.3 (searched when not exact)
--tokens N
tokens in one request: question, documents, conversation and answer;
e.g. 8k, 32k, 128k, 1M (default: the model's maximum); k = 1,024 tokens,
M = 1,048,576 (128k = 131,072 tokens); a token is about 0.75 words
--cache fp8|auto
the KV cache is the memory the engine keeps for each open conversation;
fp8 = half the memory, the usual production choice (default);
auto = the model's full precision
Sizing for a team (defaults in brackets):
--users N
total clients to serve: people, or AI agents/subagents working for them
(one person running 5 subagents counts as 5); e.g. --users 200, 2k = 2,000
--active P
% of users sending a request at the same moment (10); e.g. --active 20
--min-tok-s N
slowest acceptable answer speed per user, tokens/s (20); e.g. --min-tok-s 30
--max-wait S
longest acceptable wait for the first token under load, seconds
(10, or, if longer, twice the wait for the first words of one
typical request alone); e.g. --max-wait 5
--prompt-cache P
% of each request already read and reused: system prompt, shared documents,
a chat's history (0); e.g. --prompt-cache 80 for a chat
--typical-context N
tokens of a typical request, at most --tokens (half of --tokens);
